overview: Eric of Pomerania was ruler of Denmark, Norway, and Sweden in the Kalmar Union, remembered for long conflict and eventual deposition. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1397 — Crowned in Kalmar Union context; 1412 — Rules after Margaret’s death; 1439 — Deposed in Denmark and Sweden.
He died in 1459, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Eric of Pomerania was born c. 1382. His family background is usually placed in House of Griffin / Kalmar Union monarchy, though early Scandinavian genealogy can be uncertain and politically shaped.
Eric of Pomerania's early life belonged to the medieval Scandinavian world, where kinship, sea routes, church contacts, assemblies, and armed followings shaped the opportunities available to a ruler.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Eric of Pomerania, raised to rule the united Kalmar Union by his great-aunt Margaret I, is remembered as a ruler whose ambition outran his political skill. While Margaret lived he governed in her shadow; after her death he pursued aggressive policies — above all a long war against the Holstein counts and the Hanseatic League over Schleswig — that drained the union and turned its constituent realms against him.

His introduction of the Sound Dues, taxing shipping through the Øresund, showed a ruler alert to royal revenue, but his obstinacy and unpopular reliance on foreign officials alienated the Swedish and Danish nobility alike. Eventually deposed in all three kingdoms, he withdrew to Gotland, where tradition remembers him turning to piracy — a striking final image for a former union monarch.

The sources, shaped partly by the nobles who rejected him, present a stubborn and ultimately unsuccessful king, capable in matters of revenue but politically inflexible. He survives as a cautionary figure: the heir to Margaret's grand construction who lacked her subtlety and lived to see the union turn against him.

contentSections.title: As ruler of the Kalmar Union
paragraphs: Eric inherited Margaret I’s union settlement but lacked her political flexibility. His reign involved war over Schleswig, tensions with councils and towns, and growing dissatisfaction in Sweden.

As King of Denmark, King of Norway, King of Sweden, Eric of Pomerania had to turn dynastic claim into workable authority through alliances, military pressure, church support, and acceptance by regional elites.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Died at Rugenwalde in Pomerania in 1459 after losing the Scandinavian crowns and living as a Pomeranian duke.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: His career shows both the ambition and fragility of the Kalmar Union after Margaret.
Later saga, saintly, or national traditions often amplified Eric of Pomerania's reputation, so the article separates near-contemporary evidence from later memory where possible.

timeline.title: Born
timeline.description: Eric of Pomerania was born around c. 1382, but the birthplace is not securely recorded. The date is approximate, but it places the early life in the setting of Kingdom of Sweden / Kingdom of Norway.

timeline.title: Crowned in Kalmar Union context
timeline.description: Eric was crowned in 1397 within the Kalmar Union settlement, designed to bind Denmark, Norway, and Sweden under one monarchy.

timeline.title: Rules after Margaret’s death
timeline.description: After Margaret I died in 1412, Eric ruled without her political authority and increasingly faced resistance over war, taxation, and union government.

timeline.title: Deposed in Denmark and Sweden
timeline.description: Eric was deposed in Denmark and Sweden in 1439 after conflicts with councils and nobles made his union rule untenable.
